real_estate.homebuilder: One in five working-age renters paid late in 2025, and the 30-year reached 7.60%, its highest in almost three years.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage rates rose for a third straight day. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year reached 7.60% on Wednesday, up 0.02 and the highest in almost three years, and the 15-year is 7.22%, the highest since October 2023. On our five city median of $1,088,000 with 20% down, principal and interest come to $6,146 a month, $419 more than when September began at 6.89%.

Today's first chart is a new Urban Institute survey. One in five working-age renters (20.0%) paid rent late or short at some point in 2025, up from 16.5% in 2024 and the survey's first significant yearly change since it began in 2017. The jump came from middle income renters, 14.3% to 21.6%. The lower income rise the graphic going around shows (26.4% to 27.8%) is within the margin of error, so we drew it dashed.

The survey's income bands are national, so a family of three earning $53,300 to $106,600 counts as middle income, and the West was the one region where the share slipped. Our rents tell their own story. Zillow's August index puts the typical Fremont rent at $3,375, up 5.2% in a year, with Milpitas up 9.5% and Union City 6.3%, against 2.5% nationally. All five of our cities beat the national pace.

What this means for you: today's squeezed renters are tomorrow's buyers, but at 7.60% the median home costs about 1.8 times Fremont's typical rent before taxes and insurance. Rent growth is holding up for owners who lease; for buyers, the math rewards negotiating on price, and 147 of the ledger's 593 homes on the market have been listed 60 days or longer. Locally the five city ledger slipped to 675 from 691 and the board wide table fell 28 to 2,672.

• Board wide: 2,672 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 167 coming soon and 166 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 675 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 593 are on the market and 82 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 242 live, 189 active, 30 coming soon, 22 brand new and 1 back on market. The median on market list price is $1,242,633 at $771 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 30 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 177, Milpitas 107, Newark 87, Union City 62.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,088,000 at $673 a square foot. 276 homes are priced under a million, and 147 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

feature_image.alt: Two panel chart. Left: share of renters ages 18 to 64 who paid rent late or short in the past 12 months, 2024 to 2025, from the Urban Institute: lower income 26.4% to 27.8% (not statistically significant), all renters 16.5% to 20.0%, middle income 14.3% to 21.6% (highlighted, the only significant income group rise), higher income 4.9% to 6.9% (not significant). Right: Zillow typical rent, August 2026, change from a year earlier: Milpitas up 9.5% ($3,702 a month), Union City up 6.3% ($2,945), Fremont up 5.2% ($3,375), Newark up 4.7% ($3,675), Hayward up 3.0% ($2,637), U.S. up 2.5% ($1,948).
feature_image.caption: Middle income renters drove 2025's rise in late rent nationally. Here, rent rose faster than the national 2.5% in all five of our cities.
feature_image.source: Sources: Urban Institute, Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey, fielded December 2025 (September 2026 brief); Zillow Observed Rent Index, August 2026.

stocks.note: Levels are Wednesday, September 30 at the closing bell. Thursday is live: at 7:50 AM PT the S&P was 7,641.95 (-0.13%), the Dow 50,712.64 (-0.38%) and the Nasdaq 26,852.78 (-0.03%).
stocks.news:
Stocks closed the third quarter mixed Wednesday: the Dow fell 0.86% while the Nasdaq gained 0.24%. ADP said private employers added 90,000 jobs in September, up from a revised 36,000 in August. The government's report on Friday is expected to show 84,000 jobs and 4.1% unemployment.

After the bell, Micron reported fiscal fourth quarter revenue of $54.23 billion, nearly five times the $11.32 billion of a year earlier, and adjusted earnings of $33.42 a share. It guided to about $61.5 billion for the current quarter. AI data centers are buying memory as fast as it can be made, which is good news for Micron and less so for the price of your next laptop. The shares are down 1.3% this morning anyway.

economy.note: All four are Wednesday, September 30: the Treasury daily yield curve close, the COMEX December gold and silver settlements, and the ICE December Brent settlement, now the front month. Thursday is live: at 7:50 AM PT the 10-Year was near 5.29%, gold $4,204.00 (+0.41%), silver $61.64 (+1.77%) and December Brent $100.79 (+2.82%).
economy.commentary:
The 10-Year Treasury closed at 5.29% Wednesday, up three basis points and its highest close since May 14, 2002. Higher U.S. yields are pulling money into the dollar: the euro is near $1.13 this morning, its lowest in more than a year.

Today's second chart is Europe, where inflation jumped in September. Spain's harmonised rate hit 5.0%, Italy's 4.1%, France's 3.4% and Germany's 3.3%, all up from August and all above the European Central Bank's 2% target, which it has raised rates twice this year to defend. For scale, consumer prices in the U.S. and the San Francisco area both rose 3.4% in the year to August. The euro area figure comes Friday.

December gold settled up 0.17% and silver down 0.96%. As flagged yesterday, the Brent card switches to December, the new front month: it settled at $98.03, up 1.94% from its own Tuesday settle of $96.16. The newsletter's $103.50 was November's last day before it expired.

feature_image.alt: Horizontal bar chart of harmonised (HICP) annual inflation, September 2026 flash estimates, with August marked: Spain 5.0% (from 4.6%), Italy 4.1% (from 3.2%), France 3.4% (from 2.6%), Germany 3.3% (from 2.9%). A dashed line marks the ECB's 2% target. For scale, U.S. and San Francisco area consumer prices both rose 3.4% in the year to August 2026.
feature_image.caption: All four of Europe's largest economies saw inflation rise in September, each well above the ECB's 2% target. U.S. and Bay Area prices are running at 3.4%.
feature_image.source: Sources: INE, Istat, INSEE and Destatis flash estimates of September 29 and 30, 2026; U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

crypto.commentary:
Bitcoin closed the third quarter at $83,580 at 5 PM PT Wednesday, up 42.8% from June 30. That is its best quarter since late 2024 and its first winning quarter in a year, yet it ended about 33% below last October's record close and 4.5% below where 2026 began.

This morning is quiet: Bitcoin is up 0.16% over 24 hours, Ether up 0.34% and XRP down 1.15%, live from Coinbase at 7:50 AM PT.
